runtime_context: For Node.js use CDS 10.2 and Node.js 24 with ESM. For Java use CAP Java SDK 5.0; generated linkedInterfaces=true unless the task says otherwise. Where project configuration is not supplied, state assumptions and avoid universal diagnoses. Use the supplied fixtures for existing-project tasks.

evals.name: helpdesk-model
evals.prompt: Set up a new CAP Node.js helpdesk project and provide its domain model and service. Tickets need title, description, priority (low/medium/high), status (open/in-progress/resolved), and an assignee. Use a sensible representation for assignees and enforce the listed supplied priority/status values. Do not add a demo app or deployment features.
evals.expected_output: Valid initialization and coherent CDS domain/service definitions with the requested fields and enforced code values.
expectations: Provides valid CAP Node.js initialization without unrelated demo/deployment scaffolding; named-directory and current-directory initialization are both acceptable.
Defines all requested ticket fields with valid keys and a coherent assignee representation/relationship.
Exposes the intended ticket domain through valid service definitions with consistent names and references.
Actually enforces the supplied priority/status value sets; a bare unenforced enum is insufficient.

evals.name: close-transition-review
evals.expected_output: Finds overbroad guard and check/write race; preserves generic behavior or implements the intended update exactly once.
expectations: Identifies that the existing handler blocks unrelated updates instead of guarding only the closing transition.
Identifies the check/write race and provides valid atomic conditional update, locking, or equivalent concurrency control.
Preserves target selection and performs the intended update exactly once rather than updating in before and then letting a second generic UPDATE run.
Provides meaningful failed-transition/missing-target behavior using an affected-row check appropriate to the execution API or an equivalent supported mechanism.

evals.name: enum-and-required-title
evals.prompt: In CAP Node.js, Tickets.priority must accept only supplied values 'low', 'medium', or 'high', while Tickets.title must be required and nonempty. Priority itself may be omitted. Should I write a handler? Show the CDS solution.
evals.expected_output: Declarative mandatory-title and enforced enum validation without making optional priority mandatory.
expectations: Uses declarative required/nonempty title validation, normally @mandatory.
Enforces allowed priority values server-side, normally enum plus @assert.range: true; enum definition alone does not pass.
Keeps priority optional and avoids an unnecessary custom validation handler.

evals.name: todo-bound-action
evals.prompt: Build a small CAP Node.js todo app. Provide project commands, CDS files and the handler. Todos have a title, done flag, and optional due date. Add a bound markDone action that updates only the addressed todo, returns it, and reports a missing target meaningfully.
evals.expected_output: Consistent model/service/action and ESM handler implementing the requested target, update and return behavior.
expectations: Defines the requested fields, nullable due date, valid keys and matching service exposure.
Declares and registers a compatible bound action using the intended service implementation discovery.
The proposed action updates only the addressed todo to done=true and returns/completes according to its declaration.
Handles missing target with a meaningful client error and preserves generic service handlers, including super.init() when overriding ApplicationService.init().

evals.name: node-business-validation-error
evals.expected_output: Supported business validation with a suitable client status; does not falsely deny CAP exception handling.
expectations: Explains that an unclassified Error gives unsuitable business/client-error semantics, without claiming CAP cannot handle exceptions.
Uses supported client-error rejection or correct error aggregation to prevent invalid CREATE writes.
Retains rejection for absent/empty items and acceptance for a nonempty item array.

evals.name: node-conditional-timestamp
evals.prompt: In CAP Node.js CDS 10.2, when Tickets.status is 'resolved', resolvedAt must be non-null. Other statuses may omit it. Show a declarative rule, explain its success/failure semantics, and discuss PATCH that changes only status or clears only resolvedAt. An existing resolvedAt omitted from PATCH must be retained.
evals.expected_output: Correct message-producing expression constraint checking effective row state including partial updates.
expectations: Provides a correct declarative constraint whose violation is resolved status AND null timestamp, returning a message/key on violation and null on success.
Accepts resolved with timestamp and other status without timestamp; does not reverse valid and invalid cases.
Explains effective-state validation for status-only PATCH, timestamp-only clearing, and retaining an existing omitted timestamp rather than checking only req.data.

evals.name: java-bookshop-model
evals.prompt: Set up a CAP Java bookshop project. Provide commands and domain/service CDS files. Books have title, price, integer stock and an association to Authors; Authors have name and dateOfBirth. Avoid an unrelated demo app. State build/run assumptions rather than making claims about all Maven projects.
evals.expected_output: Java initialization, coherent CDS definitions and applicable build/run instructions.
expectations: Initializes a Java CAP project with --java, using a valid target directory, without unrelated demo scaffolding.
Defines every requested Books/Authors field, appropriate types/keys and a valid association.
Exposes the intended entities through coherent service definitions.
Provides build/code-generation and run guidance for the assumed generated project without asserting all submodule Maven goals universally fail.

evals.name: java-stock-handler-review
evals.expected_output: Identifies event mismatch, unsupported keys(), actual linked-result mismatch and stock race; proposes guarded atomic action handling.
expectations: Recognizes that CdsUpdateEventContext registers UPDATE, not submitOrder, and proposes the correct generated action context/registration and completion.
Replaces unsupported segment.keys() with supported model-aware key extraction, such as CqnAnalyzer.targetKeys().
Identifies lost updates and proposes concurrency-safe stock adjustment including a nonnegative-stock/availability guard and meaningful zero-row failure.
Handles linked typed Select results compatibly with SDK 5.0 (var/CdsResult or supported untyped conversion), without claiming this exact return typing applies to every configuration.

evals.name: java-price-validation
evals.prompt: In CAP Java Books, price must be between 0.01 and 9999.99 inclusive and title is required/nonempty. Price may be omitted. Should I write a @Before handler? Provide CDS validation.
evals.expected_output: Mandatory title and inclusive declarative range without making optional price mandatory.
expectations: Uses declarative mandatory/nonempty title validation.
Uses valid declarative inclusive price range [0.01, 9999.99] with a suitable decimal type.
Avoids an unnecessary handler and retains the requested optionality of price.

evals.name: java-submit-order-action
evals.prompt: Provide a small CAP Java bookshop implementation with Books, Authors and a CatalogService for browsing. Add an unbound submitOrder(book: UUID, quantity: Integer) action that decrements stock and returns the remaining stock. Reject nonpositive quantity, missing books and insufficient stock, including concurrent orders. Include local mock-user configuration and the security prerequisites. Use SDK 5.0 and inspect/describe generated context names rather than assuming names for bound actions.
evals.expected_output: Coherent Java model/action, guarded atomic decrement, action completion and local authentication configuration.
expectations: Provides consistent Java project/model/service/action declarations with the requested entities and return type.
Validates positive quantity and uses valid concurrency-safe stock arithmetic with sufficient-stock and missing-target handling.
Completes/returns action results consistently and uses meaningful supported client-error handling.
Provides supported local mock users/roles and available Spring Security prerequisites without claiming a direct dependency addition is always needed.

evals.name: java-validation-registration
evals.expected_output: Correct CqnService constant, CREATE-specific registration and valid error handling; precise event/entity inference.
expectations: Corrects CdsService.EVENT_CREATE to the standard CqnService event constant API.
Keeps registration specifically for CREATE on Orders, either explicitly or with a typed CdsCreateEventContext.
Explains that List<Orders> can infer entity but not CREATE by itself; does not recommend dropping the event without a typed context.
Provides supported client-error handling (ServiceException or Messages aggregation) for absent/empty items while accepting valid items.

evals.name: java-conditional-timestamp
evals.prompt: On current CAP Java SDK 5.0 with expression constraints supported, Orders with status='confirmed' must have confirmedAt. Other statuses may omit it. Show a declarative rule and valid/invalid CREATE and PATCH examples, including a PATCH that only clears confirmedAt and one that retains an existing omitted timestamp.
evals.expected_output: Correct conditional constraint and effective-state partial-update explanation.
expectations: Uses a correct declarative message-producing constraint for confirmed AND null confirmedAt, returning null for valid rows.
Accepts confirmed with timestamp and other states without timestamp; gives matching valid/invalid examples.
Covers status-only PATCH, timestamp clearing and retained omitted existing timestamps through effective-state validation rather than payload-only checking.

evals.name: java-startup-diagnostics
evals.prompt: My CAP Java app seems broken. I ran mvn spring-boot:run -pl srv from the project root and GET http://localhost:8080/odata/v4/ returned 404. I have not supplied the POM, service model or Maven log. What can we conclude, what should we inspect, and how should I verify readiness?
evals.expected_output: Evidence-based diagnosis separating Maven configuration from endpoint selection, without universal claims.
expectations: Does not conclude -pl srv or all submodule Maven commands must fail without inspecting actual logs/POM/reactor configuration.
Explains that an adapter-base-path 404 alone neither establishes application failure nor identifies a Maven error.
Derives or requests the configured service/metadata endpoint or an installed health endpoint instead of inventing an assured service path.
Distinguishes successful authenticated service/health checks from 401/connection failures without treating a 401 as proof of database/service readiness.

evals.name: java-bound-target-keys
evals.expected_output: Model-aware bound target key extraction and distinction from root keys.
expectations: Identifies unsupported segment.keys() and avoids ad hoc first-segment key extraction.
Uses supported model-aware introspection, normally CqnAnalyzer.analyze(context.getCqn()).targetKeys().
Distinguishes target order keys from root customer keys and accommodates the actual generated context name.

evals.name: existing-esm-extension
evals.prompt: Extend the supplied esm-helpdesk CAP Node.js project with a bound archive action that sets archived=true, returns the addressed ticket and rejects a missing target. Preserve ESM, existing CREATE validation and generic reads. Provide complete revised files; do not reinitialize the project. Verify a successful archive, a missing target, and existing CREATE/read behavior through the service.
evals.expected_output: Incremental ESM-compatible change preserving existing behavior and handler discovery.
expectations: Preserves ESM, existing files/model names and CREATE validation without reinitializing or converting to CommonJS.
Keeps matching service/handler discovery and super.init() so generic reads continue to work.
Declares/implements a matching bound archive action that updates only its target and returns the declared result.
Provides meaningful missing-target handling using supported API-specific result checks.

evals.name: related-row-null-validation
evals.prompt: In a CDS 10.2 CAP service, Travel has ID and currency; Booking has ID, optional currency and a required managed to-one Travel association. When Booking.currency is supplied, it must equal its existing Travel.currency. Missing Booking.currency is allowed. Add server-side constraints and show matching, mismatching, missing-currency and invalid-Travel CREATE examples. Discuss PATCH that changes only the association or currency. Do not promise revalidation of every Booking when Travel itself is changed.
evals.expected_output: Declarative association existence and currency comparison with explicit null and write-path scope.
expectations: Ensures required Travel association and target existence using supported constraints.
Enforces supplied Booking currency matching related Travel currency with a correct association-path expression.
Allows omitted/null Booking currency and gives correct valid/invalid examples without a bare null-sensitive comparison being claimed to require it.
Covers effective Booking state for PATCH and does not claim Travel-only updates automatically revalidate all children.

evals.name: concurrent-email-uniqueness
evals.prompt: Drivers must have a unique nonempty email. Two registrations with the same email can arrive concurrently. Provide domain/service CDS constraints and explain how you would test them. Updating an existing driver's displayName without changing email must still work. A SELECT-before-INSERT check alone is insufficient.
evals.expected_output: Persistence-level uniqueness plus required input; self-updates remain valid and race-safe protection is explained.
expectations: Places a named @assert.unique email constraint on the persistence entity or supplies equivalent concurrency-safe database uniqueness.
Provides required/nonempty email input validation.
Does not rely on check-before-write as the sole uniqueness protection and explains concurrent duplicate rejection.
Preserves unrelated self-updates and proposes tests for concurrent duplicates and unchanged-email updates.

evals.name: meaningful-related-seed-data
evals.prompt: Provide CSV demonstration data for namespace demo: Authors { key ID: UUID; name: String; } and Books { key ID: UUID; title: String; stock: Integer; author: Association to Authors; }. Existing author ID 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 is named Existing Author; existing book ID 22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222 is titled Existing Book, stock 5, and references that author. Preserve both existing rows. Produce final data with four authors and twelve books total, all valid author references, exactly two books with stock 0, one non-ASCII title, and one title containing a comma. Show complete correctly named CSV files; generation tools are optional.
evals.expected_output: Complete valid data preserving existing records, exact counts/scenarios and referential integrity.
expectations: Provides complete CSVs with four author rows and twelve book rows total, preserving the supplied existing rows/IDs.
Uses unique valid UUIDs and every book author_ID resolves to one of the four author IDs.
Contains exactly two stock=0 books, at least one non-ASCII title and a correctly quoted title containing a comma.
Uses correct demo-Authors.csv / demo-Books.csv naming and columns including the managed association foreign key author_ID.

evals.name: java-service-tier-typed-results
evals.prompt: In CAP Java SDK 5.0 with generated linkedInterfaces=true, a controller writes Books through PersistenceService and our CatalogService @Before validation never runs. Show how to route that business write through the application service, while keeping an intentional internal atomic stock adjustment inside submitOrder at the persistence tier. Also review Result r = db.run(Select.from(Books_.class)); for these generated types. Do persistence writes bypass managed-data handling too?
evals.expected_output: Application-service business writes, intentional persistence arithmetic, compatible typed results and accurate persistence-generic scope.
expectations: Routes the controller business write through the intended CatalogService application service so its handler chain/authorization runs.
Keeps intentional concurrency-safe internal stock arithmetic at the persistence tier and avoids recursive application-service UPDATE handling.
Uses compatible linked-interface result typing or supported untyped conversion for the supplied SDK/configuration.
Explicitly recognizes PersistenceService still runs persistence generic providers such as managed-data handling rather than claiming all generic behavior is bypassed.

evals.name: authorized-external-risk-action
evals.prompt: Add a bound assessRisk action to this CAP Node.js Orders service. Orders have UUID ID, ownerID: String and riskScore: Integer. Customers may READ only their own orders; risk-analyst users may READ all orders and call assessRisk. Neither role gets generic write permission. The action calls the supplied async getRisk(order) helper returning {score: integer}, stores the returned score for its addressed order and returns the score. Handle a missing order or provider failure without storing a fabricated/partial score. Show CDS authorization and the ESM handler; use the supplied helper, do not add a real provider integration.
evals.expected_output: Correct role/instance restrictions with necessary asynchronous action handler and failure-safe persistence.
expectations: Enforces customer own-order READ and analyst READ/action access declaratively without granting generic writes or using hardcoded user identities.
Declares/registers a matching bound action and calls getRisk for only the addressed existing order.
Stores and returns the actual valid provider score using intentional persistence work inside the authorized action.
Rejects missing order/provider failure meaningfully without fabricating or persisting a score, and preserves generic reads.

evals.name: generic-status-transitions
evals.prompt: Model a CAP Travel service with status Open='O', Accepted='A', Rejected='X'. New travels start Open; clients must not set status directly. Bound acceptTravel/rejectTravel actions may run only from Open and persist the new state. Use current generic status-transition support, without handwritten state-check/update handlers. Explain Node.js and Java setup, rejected/repeated calls, extra custom preconditions, and whether this controls CRUD or draft actions. Provide the CDS model and a service-level test matrix.
evals.expected_output: Complete @flow.status/@from/@to model, runtime setup and service-level success/rejection/rollback tests with accurate limitations.
expectations: Provides valid enum/default/read-only status and matching bound actions, using @flow.status and enum-valued @from/@to rather than replacing generic state checks/updates with handlers.
Explains Open-to-Accepted/Rejected persistence and invalid or repeated entry returning 409 with unchanged state; includes matching service-level test cases.
Distinguishes built-in Node.js support from Java cds-feature-flow runtime dependency and qualifies support for older runtimes.
Keeps authorization and additional preconditions separate; does not claim flow annotations control CRUD/DRAFT operations or allow transitions on draft instances.

evals.name: awaited-served-initialization
evals.prompt: With the standard CAP Node.js CDS 10.2 server, we need async loadRules() to finish and installRules(services, rules) to complete before the HTTP listener starts. Current code launches detached work: cds.on('served', services => { loadRules().then(rules => installRules(services, rules)) }). Can a served listener be async? Show correct startup gating and explain how initialization failure is handled. Do not invent a separate server or assume every lifecycle event is asynchronous.
evals.expected_output: Async served listener returns/awaits initialization; current standard server awaits it before listening and rejects failed initialization.
expectations: Accurately states that current served listeners support asynchronous initialization and are awaited by the standard server before HTTP listening.
Provides an async listener or returned promise that awaits both loadRules and installRules, without detached background initialization.
Propagates initialization failure through the awaited startup work rather than swallowing it, and does not generalize this contract to every lifecycle event.
